title: Renderer re-warps at the clock's tempo after it settles and reuses cached renders
description:
## Intent
Re-warp the arrangement at the clock's tempo and land it at the next bar line; reuse cached renders. Makes the re-warp, ramp, return-to-tempo, re-pitched and seconds-position scenarios of apricitus-91ed40 green.

## Steps
1. `crates/apricity-engine/src/render.rs`: arrange a `Timeline` at a given tempo (a tempo override; positions stay in score beats, re-pitched clips keep their speed). The cache key already includes the tempo-dependent length, so a returning tempo reuses renders: prove it with `ArrangeStats { rendered: 0 }`.
2. `crates/apricity-engine/src/clock.rs`: a control-side tempo watcher: request a re-render once the tempo has held for the debounce (proposal 250 ms), cancel a stale one, load with `SwapAt::NextBar`.
3. Explain the tempo in the arrangement report (score tempo vs clock tempo) so callers (M2, M3) can print it.

## Verify
`cargo test -p apricity-engine` (every `features/link/clock.feature` scenario green), and `cargo test -p apricity-score` unchanged.

Commit: `feat(<this task id>): re-warp at the clock's tempo`.

## Protocol
Specs first, watched red; log decisions, problems and outcomes with `kbs comment`; run Verify and paste the tail. Every Bash call starts `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH && cd /Users/home/Projects/Apricity`; cargo with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2` under `safe-run.sh --`. Never change dependencies to make a build pass. Sub-agents never commit, push or close.
